q1: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2: SELECT CLASS FROM ( SELECT CLASS, COUNT(DISTINCT STUDENT) AS COUNT FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS ) AS FOO WHERE COUNT >= 5
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT CLASS FROM ( SELECT CLASS, COUNT(DISTINCT STUDENT) AS COUNT FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS ) AS FOO WHERE COUNT >= 5
explanation: Both queries aim to find classes that have at least 5 students enrolled. Q1 directly groups by CLASS and checks the count of rows (i.e., students) in each class. Q2 first groups by CLASS and counts the distinct students in each class, then filters for classes with at least 5 students. Since both queries are essentially counting students in each class and filtering for a minimum count, they are semantically equivalent.
